title: Build an ISE policy set for wired access
domain: Secure Network Access, Visibility, and Enforcement
blurb: Add the switch to ISE, then write the authentication and authorization rules that decide who gets on.
purpose: The switch only asks the question; ISE gives the answer. This lab builds the ISE policy set that decides what each wired device gets, using conditions, identity stores and authorization profiles. It covers how ISE policy is put together, which shows up all over the SCOR exam.
scenario: SW1 (management address **10.10.0.2**) now sends 802.1X and MAB requests to ISE. Build the ISE side: add SW1 as a network device, create a policy set for wired traffic, and write rules so that employees get full access with the **Employees** security group, known printers get a printer profile, and everything else is denied.
objectives: Add SW1 as a network access device
Create a policy set that matches wired 802.1X and MAB
Choose the identity sources for 802.1X and MAB
Write authorization rules and predict which one matches

steps.title: Add the switch as a network device
steps.learn: ISE answers RADIUS only from devices it knows. Each network access device (NAD) has a name, an IP address and the **same shared secret** that the switch uses.
steps.task: Add SW1: name **SW1**, IP address **10.10.0.2**, device type **All Device Types**, RADIUS authentication turned on, shared secret **R4diusKey**.
steps.screen: ISE › Administration › Network Resources › Network Devices › Add
steps.hint: The shared secret is the key you set on the switch with `radius server ISE`.

steps.title: Create the policy set
steps.learn: A **policy set** is the top-level match. ISE checks policy sets top-down, and the first set whose condition matches handles the request. Inside it, the **allowed protocols** list decides which EAP methods ISE will accept.
steps.task: Create the policy set **Wired-Access**. Match the built-in conditions for wired 802.1X **or** wired MAB, and allow **Default Network Access**.
steps.hint: The library has compound conditions named Wired_802.1X and Wired_MAB. Combine them with OR.

steps.title: Choose the identity sources
steps.learn: The **authentication policy** decides where identities are checked. 802.1X users are checked against **Active Directory**. MAB requests carry only a MAC address, so they're checked against **Internal Endpoints**. For MAB, "If User not found" is usually set to **CONTINUE**, so unknown devices still reach the authorization rules, for example to get a guest or remediation result instead of a hard failure.
steps.task: Set the Dot1X rule to use the **scor_AD** join point. Set the MAB rule to use **Internal Endpoints**, with **CONTINUE** when the user isn't found.
steps.screen: ISE › Policy Sets › Wired-Access › Authentication Policy

fields.label: MAB rule › If User not found

steps.title: Write the employee rule
steps.learn: **Authorization rules** are also checked top-down, and the first match wins. A result combines an **authorization profile** (access type, VLAN, dACL) and, with TrustSec, a **security group** (SGT).
steps.task: Create the rule **Employees**: condition AD group **scor.lab/Users/Employees**, profile **PermitAccess**, security group **Employees**.
steps.screen: ISE › Policy Sets › Wired-Access › Authorization Policy › Insert new row above

steps.title: Order the rules
steps.learn: Specific rules go above general ones, and the Default rule is always last.
steps.task: Put the authorization rules in the order ISE should check them.
steps.question: Order the rules from top to bottom.
items: Employees: AD group Employees → PermitAccess, SGT Employees
Printers: endpoint identity group Printers → Cisco_Printer_Profile, SGT Printers

steps.title: Predict the result
steps.question: A contractor's laptop authenticates with valid AD credentials. The account is in the **Contractors** group, not **Employees**. Which result does ISE return?

options.why: Authentication proves who the user is. Authorization still needs a rule to match, and only Default does.

options.text: The printer profile, because it's the next rule down.
options.why: The Printers rule matches an endpoint identity group, which this laptop isn't in.
The credentials are valid, so authentication passes. It's the authorization result that denies access.

summary: SW1 added as a network device, the Wired-Access policy set for wired 802.1X and MAB, AD for 802.1X and Internal Endpoints for MAB, and authorization rules for employees, printers and a deny default.
